designSequence.waveName: Step Callable, StepExecutionResult, Optional Result Contributions

purpose: Define a closed, typed, independently optional contribution model for the Step-level validation, error, and error-handling aggregates. The design preserves specialized result ownership and keeps optional Supporting Pattern dependencies out of the mandatory Core import path.

included: The OptionalResultContributions aggregate and its three baseline result categories.
Generic type relationships between OptionalResultContributions and StepExecutionResult.
Independent optionality, type safety, result provenance, and custody semantics.
The distinction between result absence, negative domain conclusions, invocation failure, and operational state.
The exclusion of Observation Unit output from the common Step result.
Dependency, Public API, serialization, and conformance requirements.
excluded: The internal behavior of Validator Units, Error Handling Units, or Step Error Models.
A generic Error Model or generic error taxonomy.
A universal Supporting Unit base class or common result inheritance hierarchy.
An open-ended runtime-discovered contribution set, plugin manager, registry, or untyped dictionary.
Observation events, logs, telemetry, or Observation Unit results as common Step result contributions.
A universal serialization format or result storage manager.

governingPrinciples.optionalMeansOptional: A Step may select none, one, or multiple optional Supporting Pattern capabilities. The Core Step result contract must not require installation or import of any optional pattern package.
governingPrinciples.semanticOwnership: Each optional aggregate retains the semantic ownership and schema defined by its specialized contract. OptionalResultContributions groups values for transport through the Step result; it does not redefine their meaning.
governingPrinciples.independentSlots: Each known result category is independently present or absent. The presence or absence of one category does not determine another category.
governingPrinciples.absenceIsNotStatus: An absent slot does not mean success, failure, NotApplicable, NotExecuted, or any other universal status.
governingPrinciples.typedNotDynamic: The contribution bundle is statically typed by the concrete Step specialization. It is not a dynamic collection keyed by strings or discovered through a runtime registry.
governingPrinciples.observationSeparation: Observation is a separate optional capability whose output is independent of the Step result aggregates. Observation records remain outside this common contribution bundle.
governingPrinciples.resultCustody: A contribution is included as Present only after its value has been produced and accepted into Step custody under its specialized contract.

architecturalOptions.name: DirectOptionalFieldsOnStepResult
architecturalOptions.description: Keep validatorResult, errorResult, and errorHandlerResult as independent top-level generic fields on StepExecutionResult.
advantages: Closest to the existing serialized field layout.
disadvantages: Scatters the optional contribution contract across the main Step result.
Does not provide one cohesive typed boundary for the set of optional results.
Makes future reviewed contribution-set evolution less localized.

architecturalOptions.name: UntypedDictionary
architecturalOptions.description: Represent optional results as dict[str, object], dict[str, Any], or equivalent string-keyed payloads.
advantages: Accepts arbitrary values without declaring generic type parameters.
disadvantages: Loses static type safety and stable field semantics.
Allows misspelled, duplicated, unknown, or incompatible keys.
Encourages consumers and integrations to rely on undocumented runtime conventions.

architecturalOptions.name: RuntimeContributionRegistry
architecturalOptions.description: Register contribution providers and result types dynamically and discover them at runtime.
disadvantages: Introduces a plugin/registry subsystem that GPWCF does not own.
Makes optional pattern participation depend on runtime discovery and registration.
Creates lifecycle, identity, compatibility, and ordering concerns not established by the result contract.

architecturalOptions.name: TypedClosedContributionBundle
architecturalOptions.description: Use one immutable OptionalResultContributions value object with a fixed set of named, independently typed optional slots for the existing Step-level aggregates.
advantages: Preserves the current specialized result categories and their independent optionality.
Avoids concrete optional-pattern imports through generic type parameters.
Provides one stable and explicit contribution boundary.
Avoids runtime registries, string keys, and untyped payloads.
disadvantages: A new contribution category requires an explicit reviewed contract revision.
The existing StepExecutionResult field layout must be revised to contain the bundle.

selectedDesign.decision: Adopt a closed generic OptionalResultContributions value object with three named optional result slots, each represented through OptionalResultSlot[T] = Absent | Present[T].

aggregatePresence.rule: Every StepExecutionResult contains one OptionalResultContributions value object.
aggregatePresence.reason: This keeps the result envelope structurally stable and prevents the aggregate object's own absence from being confused with the independent absence of its three contribution categories.
aggregatePresence.allAbsentMeaning: A bundle whose three slots are Absent means that no values for these categories are included in this StepExecutionResult. It does not establish whether a pattern was selected, attempted, applicable, or successful.

slotModel.name: OptionalResultSlot[T]

variants.name: Absent
variants.meaning: No value of this category is included in the StepExecutionResult.
invariants: Absence is not a success/failure or applicability status.
Absence does not prove that the corresponding capability was not selected or not executed.
A result type specialized to typing.Never must always use Absent.

variants.name: Present[T]
variants.representation: An immutable wrapper containing exactly one value of type T.
variants.meaning: A value was produced and accepted into Step custody and is included in the StepExecutionResult.
invariants: The wrapped value conforms to the concrete Step specialization's declared result type.
The wrapped value may itself be None if T permits None.
Presence does not imply that the represented domain conclusion is successful.

slotModel.whyNotNone: Using None as the sole absence marker is ambiguous when the specialized domain result type itself permits None. The discriminated Absent/Present representation distinguishes an absent slot from Present(None).
slotModel.implementationForm: A small immutable algebraic/discriminated value type. The exact Python classes, singleton construction, pattern-matching surface, and serialization tags are implementation details to be finalized after architecture acceptance.

contributionSlots.specializedMeaning: StepValidatorResult: the Step-level validation result or aggregate produced from applicable Validator Unit Validation Results.
contributionSlots.semanticOwner: Concrete Step validation specialization and Step Composition.
contributionSlots.producer: Step Composition aggregates accepted Validator Unit Validation Results under the concrete Step rules.
constraints: The slot contains the Step-level aggregate, not an individual Validator Unit Validation Result by default.
A negative validation conclusion is a normally produced validation result and is not automatically an invocation failure.
A thrown Validator Unit invocation exception does not fabricate a validator_result value.
The concrete Step defines the aggregation structure and the meaning of each outcome.

contributionSlots.specializedMeaning: The Step-level ErrorResult aggregate defined by the concrete Step Error Model.
contributionSlots.producer: Step Composition physically aggregates eligible error occurrences according to the selected Step Error Model.
constraints: The generic Core slot does not define error types, occurrences, registries, categories, severity, or retry semantics.
The current Generator Common Error Model remains consumer-specific and is not imported by Core.
An exception that prevents a result-producing operation from returning does not automatically create an ErrorResult value.
The concrete Step Error Model defines the exact aggregation and provenance semantics.

contributionSlots.specializedMeaning: The Step-level ErrorHandlerResult aggregate of accepted error-handling operation entries and their occurrence targets.
contributionSlots.semanticOwner: Step-specific Error Handling Composition and the selected Error Handling Unit contracts.
contributionSlots.producer: The Step-specific Error Handling Composition aggregates accepted operation entries; Step Composition integrates the aggregate.
constraints: It represents handling-operation records/results and does not by itself assert that an error was resolved.
It does not contain, mutate, remove, or subsume ErrorResult.
Publication acceptance, indeterminate outcomes, recovery ownership, and custody remain governed by OperationEntryPublisher and the applicable Single Step Publication specialization.

genericParameters.name: TValidatorResult
genericParameters.specialization: The concrete StepValidatorResult aggregate type, or typing.Never when the Step does not select a validator result contribution.

genericParameters.name: TErrorResult
genericParameters.specialization: The concrete Step ErrorResult type, or typing.Never when the Step does not select a Step Error Model contribution.

genericParameters.name: TErrorHandlerResult
genericParameters.specialization: The concrete ErrorHandlerResult type, or typing.Never when the Step does not select the Error Handling contribution.

typeSpecializationRules.neverRule: When a capability is not selected, its generic result parameter is typing.Never and its slot is statically constrained to Absent. This avoids importing an optional pattern result package for a Step that does not use it.
typeSpecializationRules.selectedButNoValueRule: When a capability is selected but no value was produced and accepted for this invocation, the slot remains Absent. The concrete Step's own specialization and execution evidence determine applicability and execution facts; the slot itself does not encode them.
typeSpecializationRules.noRuntimeDiscovery: The generic parameters are fixed by the concrete Step specialization. They are not selected by a runtime registry, plugin scan, or dynamic import.

constructionAndCustody.constructionOwner: Step Composition, through the owning Step Aggregate.
constructionRules: Create Present(value) only after the corresponding specialized result has been produced and accepted into Step custody.
Use Absent when no value of that category is included in the returned StepExecutionResult.
Preserve the exact specialized value and its producer/invocation provenance; do not normalize it into a common result schema.
Do not create an ErrorHandlerResult from ErrorResult merely because the same error occurrence is referenced.
Do not infer validator_result from SPUExecutionResult or infer error_result from a thrown exception.
Do not fabricate a contribution for an operation that did not return its declared result.
If handoff acceptance is indeterminate, retain the unresolved custody fact under the specialized recovery contract; do not mark the slot Present until acceptance is established.
constructionAndCustody.afterLaterFailure: If the Step invocation later throws and no StepExecutionResult can be returned, accepted contribution values remain preserved in StepCompositionFlowResult or the concrete recovery/custody mechanism. They are not wrapped in a fabricated partial StepExecutionResult.
constructionAndCustody.postReturnCustody: After StepExecutionResult is returned, the result bundle and accepted values remain valid under the Step result retention contract, independently of later Step instance reuse or retirement.

explicitlyExcludedCategories.reason: It is a per-SPU invocation result consumed internally by Step Composition. It is not an optional Step-level Supporting Pattern aggregate.
It is internal Step invocation evidence, not a Stage-facing result contribution.

explicitlyExcludedCategories.category: ObservationRecord and Observation Unit activity results
explicitlyExcludedCategories.reason: Observation output is independent of the Step result categories and is explicitly excluded by the Observation Unit and StepExecutionResult contracts.

explicitlyExcludedCategories.category: Prefect State and native runtime results
explicitlyExcludedCategories.reason: They are operational execution evidence, not GPWCF domain contributions.
Generic Diagnostics is a separate Wave 4 design decision; it must not be smuggled into this optional contribution bundle.

futureExtensionPolicy.rule: The baseline contribution set is closed to the three existing Step-level result categories.
futureExtensionPolicy.addingCategory: A new category requires a separately reviewed specialized contract, a declared owner, a generic type slot decision, dependency-closure analysis, and an explicit versioned revision of OptionalResultContributions and StepExecutionResult.
prohibitedShortcuts: Do not add arbitrary extras dictionaries.
Do not add string-keyed result maps.
Do not add a runtime contribution registry or plugin discovery.
Do not add a universal SupportingUnitResult base class merely to make the bundle heterogeneous.
Do not import every optional Supporting Pattern package into Core.

stepExecutionResultIntegration.presence: Required aggregate object; its individual slots are independently Absent or Present.
stepExecutionResultIntegration.processingArtifact: Remains a separate OptionalResultSlot[TOutput] field on StepExecutionResult and is not part of OptionalResultContributions.
stepExecutionResultIntegration.identity: StepExecutionResult carries Step and parent Stage invocation identities separately from the contribution payloads.
stepExecutionResultIntegration.semanticRule: The contribution bundle groups the optional result values for transport and typed access. It does not alter the semantics or ownership of any specialized result.

coreDependencies: Python standard library typing/value-object primitives only.
forbiddenDependencies: A dynamic plugin or result registry.
A universal core.shared_contracts or core.results package.
dependencyAndPackageAllocation.optionalPatternDependencyDirection: Concrete Step specializations import only the optional pattern contracts they select and supply their specialized result types as generic parameters. The generic contribution container does not import those patterns.
dependencyAndPackageAllocation.identityDependency: StepExecutionResult identity fields use canonical core.identities value types; OptionalResultContributions itself has no identity service or runtime dependency.

publicApi.stability: These are supported public contracts after Wave 2 acceptance. Internal constructor helpers and serialization adapters remain private unless explicitly added to the Public API design.

prefectAndSerializationBoundary.coreRule: Core contribution values are typed domain values and do not prescribe a wire format.
prefectAndSerializationBoundary.prefectRule: Prefect Integration must preserve Absent versus Present, including Present(None), when persisting/retrieving a StepExecutionResult across a native subworkflow boundary.
prefectAndSerializationBoundary.serializerRule: A serializer must explicitly encode the slot discriminator and the specialized payload. It must not collapse Absent and Present(None) to the same null representation.
prefectAndSerializationBoundary.specializedPayloadRule: Concrete result payload serialization remains the responsibility of the consumer/specialized contract or an explicitly selected integration codec. No dynamic codec registry is introduced.
prefectAndSerializationBoundary.operationalSeparation: Prefect State and native IDs remain separate from OptionalResultContributions and StepExecutionResult.
prefectAndSerializationBoundary.qualificationBoundary: PHASE-01/02 used fixture result objects and did not qualify production OptionalResultContributions serialization, optional pattern binding, multi-host transport, or failure/recovery custody.

conformanceRequirements.requirement: OptionalResultContributions is a typed immutable value object with the three baseline named categories.
validator_result, error_result, and error_handler_result are independently typed and independently present/absent.
The bundle itself is structurally present in StepExecutionResult; all three slots may be Absent.
Absence does not imply success, failure, non-applicability, or non-execution.
A Step that does not select a capability uses typing.Never for its result type and can only produce Absent for that slot.
A selected capability's slot becomes Present only after its specialized result is produced and accepted into Step custody.
ErrorResult and ErrorHandlerResult remain separate and retain their specialized contracts.
Validator Unit negative domain outcomes remain distinguishable from invocation failures.
SPUExecutionResult and StepCompositionFlowResult are not included as generic optional contribution categories.
Observation Unit records/events remain excluded from the common contribution bundle.
Core imports no concrete optional Supporting Pattern result packages, Generator Error Model, or Prefect.
No dynamic result registry, string-keyed map, or arbitrary extras dictionary is used.
Serialization preserves the Absent/Present discriminator and specialized payload type.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: Replace direct optional aggregate fields with the OptionalResultContributions bundle, preserve each named category as an independently optional slot, and use OptionalResultSlot for explicit presence semantics.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: Creates a cohesive typed optional contribution boundary without optional pattern imports and preserves Present(None) distinctly from absence.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.approval: Requires explicit architecture acceptance before source contract editing.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: Define the assembly/custody handoff from selected Supporting Pattern results into the corresponding typed OptionalResultContributions slots.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: Step Composition is the physical aggregator and custody owner for accepted internal results.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.approval: Requires explicit architecture acceptance before source contract editing.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: Keep StepExecutionResult and OptionalResultContributions in MOD-CORE-STEP-RESULTS; explicitly permit only generic typing/value-object dependencies and prohibit optional pattern imports.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: The module boundary must reflect the generic optional-result mechanism without coupling Core to all Supporting Patterns.

decisionsAndRationales.decision: Use a closed typed bundle rather than a dynamic contribution registry.
decisionsAndRationales.rationale: The currently established result categories are known and specialized; dynamic discovery would add an unowned plugin/runtime subsystem.
This preserves independent optionality and allows a legitimate None payload without losing presence information.

decisionsAndRationales.decision: Keep the contribution bundle structurally present in every StepExecutionResult.
decisionsAndRationales.rationale: A stable envelope with independently absent slots avoids giving the bundle itself a second ambiguous applicability/absence meaning.

decisionsAndRationales.decision: Keep Observation Unit outputs outside the common bundle.
decisionsAndRationales.rationale: The Observation contract explicitly separates observation records from validation, error, error handling, and Step result semantics.

decisionsAndRationales.decision: Require explicit versioned review for new contribution categories.
decisionsAndRationales.rationale: Prevents the generic result model from turning into an unbounded universal result container.

supports: The three optional aggregate categories and their independent optionality.
Absence does not imply success/failure or applicability.
Observation results are excluded by default.
SPUExecutionResult is an internal per-SPU result and not a Step-level optional aggregate.
ErrorHandlerResult is an aggregate of accepted handling operation entries.
ErrorHandlerResult is distinct from ErrorResult and does not by itself establish resolution.
Validator Unit Validation Result is produced per normally completed invocation.
Step Composition aggregates accepted validator results into a StepValidatorResult.
Negative validation outcomes are domain results, not automatic invocation failures.
Observation records and activity results are independent of StepExecutionResult.
Observation output is not a default Step result contribution.
StepExecutionResult generic type and its OptionalResultContributions field.
OptionalResultSlot presence model and result preservation invariants.

acceptanceCriteria: OptionalResultContributions is statically typed and closed to the three established optional Step-level result categories.
Each contribution slot is independently present/absent and preserves its specialized semantic type.
A Step can omit optional pattern dependencies by specializing unused contribution types to typing.Never.
The contribution bundle does not include SPUExecutionResult, StepCompositionFlowResult, Observation output, diagnostics, or Prefect State.
The generic contribution contract does not import concrete optional Supporting Pattern or Generator-specific packages.
Result production, acceptance, custody, and recovery remain governed by the specialized contracts and Step Composition.
Serialization preserves the discriminated slot state and concrete payload.
The design is consistent with 04.00_Step_Callable.json and 05.00_Step_Execution_Result.json.
No source contract or production source package is modified by this artifact.

changeControl.authority: Wave 2 detailed design proposal. It becomes an implementation constraint only after architecture review and explicit acceptance.
changeControl.sourceContractPolicy: This artifact does not modify StepExecutionResult_Contract.json, Step_Composition_Contract.json, ErrorHandlerResult_Contract.json, or any optional pattern contract.
changeControl.implementationGate: Do not implement OptionalResultSlot or OptionalResultContributions until all Wave 2 artifacts and required governing contract changes are reviewed and accepted.
changeControl.nextStep: Wave 2 detailed design is complete at the artifact level. Validate all three Wave 2 artifacts together for signature/type/identity/optional-slot consistency before proceeding to Wave 3.
